end.summary:
Anika named the dustbin as the place for litter.
They identified apple peel as wet waste for the green bin and a plastic wrapper as dry waste for the blue bin.
They discussed that keeping school clean is a shared responsibility, including putting away the waste they create.
Anika was unsure about how air and microbes help composting; the idea that plastic also rots in a compost pit remained uncorrected at the end.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Anika practised sorting wet and dry waste, explaining green and blue bins, and discussing everyone’s role in keeping school clean, green and safe. They gave relevant examples such as apple peel, plastic wrappers, and putting litter in a dustbin. The mix-up that plastic can rot in a compost pit was still present at the end, so it was not corrected during this lesson. At home, ask Anika to sort a few household items and explain which items can compost and which must stay out of the compost pit.
